# Cache redundant whole-tree AST parsing across test scanners

## Context / Problem
Many regression-oracle tests independently walk a source tree (tests/ or src/rebar), read every
*.py, and ast.parse it. Measured: one full parse of tests/ (~1653 files) costs ~2.3s idle
(~7.6s under load) and src/rebar (~597 files) ~0.8s; dozens of test files each repeat such a
walk. The redundant PARSE is ~75-80% of each scan's cost (parse+read vs ast.walk). Under `--cov`
on the coverage cell these scanners are the top `--durations` entries (18.7-29.93s each). After
the macOS cell is reduced (sibling story omphacite-desertlike-coney, 3ba8-49d5-fee5-445d), the
Ubuntu coverage cell becomes the gate's long pole, so cutting this redundancy directly cuts the
gate.

## Approach
Add a shared, process-global memoised parse — tests/_tree_scan.py exposing
`parsed_python_files(root)` returning parsed modules, cached via functools.cache with the root
`.resolve()`d so different spellings share one cache entry. Migrate the whole-tree AST scanners
to it so the FIRST scanner per xdist worker parses a given root and every other scanner reuses it
for free. Cross-file proof (prototype, already validated): after migrating the three heaviest
tests-tree scanners the 2nd/3rd scanner dropped 6.64s->2.89s and 5.07s->1.91s with identical
pass/fail. This fits the goal — pure redundancy removal, no test weakened.

### Parse contract (why it is behaviour-preserving)
The helper standardises the parse the migrated scanners already performed, and the contract is
chosen to keep results byte-identical:
- **filename** — `ast.parse(source, filename=str(path))`, so SyntaxError text and node metadata
  match the scanners that passed `filename=str(path)` today.
- **encoding** — `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (strict). Every committed `.py` under
  src/rebar and tests is valid UTF-8, so strict decoding yields the same source the previous
  `errors="replace"` reads produced (replace only diverges on invalid bytes, of which the tree
  has none); the eager parse itself would fail loudly if that invariant ever broke.
- **SyntaxError tolerance** — the helper parses eagerly (no per-file `try/except SyntaxError`).
  The migrated scanners' guards were never-hit because the committed trees always parse; the
  shared eager parse re-asserts that same repo-parses invariant in one place.

### Scope boundary (which scanners are EXCLUDED)
Migration is limited to whole-tree scanners over the **committed** src/rebar and tests trees.
Scanners whose walk helper is ALSO invoked with synthetic/planted or tmp_path roots — which may
hold intentionally-unparseable or out-of-repo files, where `ParsedModule.relative =
path.relative_to(repo_root)` would raise or an eager parse would wrongly fail — are EXCLUDED and
keep their own path-based read+guard. Concretely excluded: tests/unit/test_run_request_builder.py,
tests/unit/test_context_hints_single_source.py, and the planted-path scan inside
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py (its committed-tree scan is migrated; its planted
scan is not). Tolerant scanners that only ever scan the committed trees
(e.g. test_review_discovery_architecture.py) have their never-hit `try/except SyntaxError:
continue` removed per the contract above.

## Scope
- tests/_tree_scan.py (NEW) — the cached `parsed_python_files(root)` helper and a `ParsedModule`
  value (path / relative / source / tree), implementing the parse contract above.
- Whole-tree `.py` AST scanners under tests/unit/, tests/unit/store/, tests/unit/commands/,
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/, and tests/interfaces/contracts/ — migrate each scanner that does
  `for p in ROOT.rglob("*.py"): ast.parse(p.read_text())` over a committed tree to the shared
  helper, preserving every per-file filter and the exact `relative_to(BASE)` base. Non-`.py`
  globs (`rglob("*")`, `*.sh`, `*.json`) and filename-only collections are left unchanged; the
  excluded planted/tmp-root scanners named above are not migrated.

## Testing
- Each migrated file's tests pass unchanged (same selection, same assertions) via
  `pytest <file> -p no:xdist`.
- The full migrated scanner set runs in one process with identical pass/fail (proves the cache
  is shared cross-file and no scanner regressed): `pytest <migrated files> -p no:xdist`.
- The excluded planted-root scanners (test_run_request_builder, test_context_hints_single_source,
  the planted scan in test_nested_pytest_uniqueness) still pass unchanged — the failure/edge path
  proving the scope boundary holds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] tests/_tree_scan.py provides `parsed_python_files(root)` returning parsed modules, memoised
      per process, using `ast.parse(source, filename=str(path))` and strict-utf-8 reads (verified
      by a same-object second-call check and by the migrated tests passing).
- [x] The whole-tree AST scanners in Scope over committed trees call the shared helper; each
      migrated file passes `pytest <file> -p no:xdist` unchanged.
- [x] The excluded planted/tmp-root scanners (test_run_request_builder.py,
      test_context_hints_single_source.py, the planted scan in test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py)
      are NOT migrated and still pass (verified by running them).
- [x] No behaviour change: the full migrated set run in one process yields the same pass/fail as
      before (verified locally green — 601 passed, 2 skipped).
- [x] Running the migrated scanner set in a single process parses each root once — a 2nd+
      same-root scanner is materially faster than a cold parse (verified by a timed probe).
- [x] ruff check + ruff format are clean on all changed files and the complexity baseline check
      passes.
